note: Des Moines County Conservation area along the Skunk River below Augusta. Camping is only at Sycamore Loop, the easternmost (downstream) loop: sites strung along a lane on the river bank, with a shelter house. Maple Loop at Augusta closed permanently at the end of 2021; Cottonwood Loop, 1.1 mi west of Augusta, is day use and a boat ramp only (no camping). --Claude
summary: County page and Sycamore Loop map: camping only at Sycamore Loop (18 sites, 12 electric), central water, RV dump, outhouses, FCFS, 14-day max; electric $20 (Sycamore section) or $25 (general line), non-electric $10. Stored pin is at the closed Maple Loop, ~1 km from Sycamore. Waterfront lead up.
flags: PIN: stored 40.75700,-91.27000 is at the east edge of Augusta by the Maple Loop (17703 Skunk River Rd geocodes to 40.7569,-91.2716), which the county says 'was permenantly closed at the end of 2021'. Sycamore Loop, the only camping loop, is ~1.0 km ESE: re-pin to ~40.7535,-91.2588 (seen on imagery: the lane, four gravel pads, the shelter house and RVs at the east end, matching the county's site map).

WATERFRONT LEAD (up): not waterfront -> riverview proposed. The stored evidence ('Skunk River ~200m S of pinned area; sites set back from river') was read at the closed Maple Loop pin, so it is not evidence for Sycamore. At Sycamore the county map and imagery show the sites strung along a lane on the north bank of the Skunk, which is ~90-100 m wide here; the lane runs between most sites and the water, with a 10-20 m strip of grass and bank shrubs/trees beyond it, so on-water is blocked by the loop road rule but a view across it is supported (NAIP 0.36 m/px). On the county map sites 4, 8, 13 and 15 are drawn on the river side of the lane; if they are, they would need a closer look for riverfront. No levee is visible.

FEES: the same county page gives two electric rates - '$25 per night' in the park-wide rate box and '$20 per night' in the Sycamore Loop box. Sycamore is the only camping loop, so one of them is stale; both kept as the range. Non-electric $10 sites are on the same drive-in lane (not tent-only), so they set the low.
